base: working copy of build/journal-gated-implementation-20261101/stage4-persistent (the bit-exact v1 reviewed build tree), plus refs/ copied for build.sh signer resolution. The v1 tree and its APK are untouched.

build.method: v2/build-v2.sh: gen_pinned_key.py regenerates Stage4PinnedProofKey.java from a DER public key, then October's stage4-persistent/app/build.sh (javac -source 8 -target 8, d8 --min-api 28, aapt2 link, apksigner v1+v2), identical toolchain to the v1 build
build.signer: upstream SnuSnuRoot public debug keystore (same as v1 and the device-installed APK, so a future approved session could upgrade in place)

gap_status_after_v2.gap1_ready_bootstrap: CLOSED host-side: genesis protocol + state machine implemented in Stage4AttemptJournalV2 (installGenesis / recoverLockoutWithGenesis), domain-separated genesis proofs (Stage4GenesisVerifier), challenge issuance is idempotent and consumed on any verification attempt. Device execution still requires the genesis session (runbook addendum Phase G).
gap_status_after_v2.gap2_proof_custody: DESIGN CLOSED, DEVICE PART OPEN: message format fixed to the compiled ECDSA stage4-root-v1; custody location (/data/snusnu_root/signer, root:root 0700/0400), signer self-attestation gating, operator-token genesis mode, and mailbox transport (app DPS drop primary, cache fallback, socket rejected) are specified in the design doc. Verifier-side pinning is implemented and build-parameterized. The device signer binary/script itself is NOT implemented: its exec context and SELinux behaviour can only be settled in the root session (design doc section 4). HostReferenceSigner.java is a test-only stand-in and must never reach a device.
gap_status_after_v2.gap3_boot_identity: CLOSED host-side as a design + code: three-layer identity (signer /proc anchor, waiter witness file, boot-count latch) implemented via Stage4BootWitness + journal v2 rules, including degraded mode and contradiction denial. Whether time_update can write the witness under Enforcing, and the app domain's real permissions, remain session-verifiable items (design doc section 4).

host_tests_2026-11-01.combined_run: 60 tests OK = the 59 baseline tests of the v1 manifest (9 modules) + the new v2 module. NOTE: the system python3 (3.9) errors on one baseline module's PEP 604 syntax; python3.14 is the project interpreter, as in the v1 session.
host_tests_2026-11-01.new_module: test_execute_firehd10_journal_v2_bootstrap_host_20261101 (project root): 19 harness scenarios, all PASS (empty-begin denial, genesis without/with challenge, wrong key, wrong build, same-boot begin denial, challenge issuance, wrong-challenge and cross-boot completion denial, completion + replay denial, lockout + genesis-only recovery, foreign-record preservation, boot-count latch, degraded identity flow, witness/kernel contradiction denial, 8-thread begin race, fsync-failure denial, strict drop/witness parsers, pinned-key roundtrip)

pinned_proof_key.label: HOST TEST KEY - NOT THE DEVICE KEY
pinned_proof_key.private_key: generated in a temp dir on the Mac for the host build, never copied into the project, deleted in the same session. NOBODY can sign a valid proof for this APK. The device key is generated on-device during the genesis session and pinned by rebuilding (runbook addendum Phase G).

purpose: v2 journal implementation closing the three host-addressable gaps of the v1 journal build (READY genesis bootstrap, proof-signer custody design + verifier-side pinning, stock-SELinux boot identity). Host-built APK, NOT installed, NOT deployment approved.
removed_from_v2_tree: Stage4AttemptJournal.java (v1 journal) is NOT present in the v2 source tree, so no build can contain two journal writers. The v2 journal uses a different state file (stage4-native-attempt-v2.state); a v1-format record is FOREIGN to it by design and a device-side v1 INFLIGHT lockout is neither interpreted nor cleared by v2.
